chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Salih ibn Khalid, from Abd al-Hamid ibn Mufaddal al-Samman, who said:
I asked a virtuous man (peace be upon him) about the ghee of oxen, and he said, 'Do not buy it and do not sell it.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: This report is consistent with the doctrine of the Waqifiyyah (those who stopped believing in the Imams after Imam Musa al-Kazim), because they believe that the meat of oxen is forbidden, so they applied the ruling of the meat to the ghee. And that is false in our view, and no attention is paid to it.

key_terms.الْوَاقِفَةُ: The Waqifiyyah, a Shia sect that stopped believing in the Imams after Musa al-Kazim

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on buying and selling ghee from oxen in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights a specific juristic nuance regarding the permissibility of ghee from oxen, contrasting the general Shia view with the stricter stance of the Waqifiyyah sect. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan clarifies that while the Waqifiyyah deemed the meat haram and thus extended this to its fat, Shia jurisprudence rejects this extension, affirming the general permissibility of the product. This distinction underscores the methodological differences in deriving rulings from primary substances to their derivatives within early Shia scholarly tradition.
